rows.notes: The cited document is a review article (title page marked REVIEW): a narrative review of UAS applications in wildlife science plus a systematic bibliometric review of wildlife journal records (counts of articles alluding to aircraft, satellites and tracking devices). Its only original data are literature-frequency counts (Section 5, Figs. 1-4), which say nothing about wildlife disturbance from UAV flights or battery disposal. The statements on disturbance (Section 2.4) summarise other studies (Sarda-Palomera et al. 2012, Chabot et al. 2015, Ditmer et al. 2015, Vas et al. 2015, etc.) and in fact conclude that UAS cause low to no disturbance, with animals habituating to repeated flybys, while noting that close-up flights elicit stronger reactions and advising caution; this is secondary synthesis, not the study's own result. Lithium-ion battery disposal is not mentioned at all. Hence Q1 is 'no' and Q2-Q9 follow as 'no'.

notes: Full text appears complete (pp. 137-155 including references). The document is a review; the embedded systematic review only quantifies literature trends and does not constitute primary evidence on the claimed wildlife-disturbance or sustainability effects of UAV flights.
